react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on Galactose Metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway in this metabolomics comparison. RaMP multi-DB ORA (SMPDB + KEGG namespaces) returns Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043 / KEGG:map00052) at rank 0 with FDR = 2.83e-11, driven by four input metabolites — galactinol, sucrose, myo-inositol, and glycerol — overlapping 4 of 31 pathway members. The same four metabolites independently hit Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) at the same extreme significance. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms the same KEGG entry (hsa00052) at rank 0 with p = 3.25e-07, validating the result against the community-standard KEGG library. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis places Galactose Metabolism at rank 4 (p = 0.016) on the KEGG-human_mfn empirical network, providing a third independent line of evidence. The m/z-paradigm additionally flags Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism, rank 6, p = 0.028) via the direct input 8(S)-HPETE, a 12-lipoxygenase product of arachidonic acid, consistent with a secondary oxidative-lipid signal. Galactinol (α-D-galactosyl-(1→3)-1D-myo-inositol) is the most pathway-discriminating driver because it is structurally unique to galactose metabolism and not a generic sugar. The simultaneous elevation of sucrose, D-glucose, glycerol and myo-inositol is consistent with Leloir-pathway substrate accumulation under conditions of perturbed galactokinase or galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase activity. Dopamine and D-glucose also appear in GPCR downstream signalling (REACT:R-HSA-388396), suggesting a secondary neurotransmitter–energy co-occurrence not supported by the strong galactose-metabolism consensus.

The same four metabolites independently hit Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) at the same extreme significance. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms the same KEGG entry (hsa00052) at rank 0 with p = 3.25e-07, validating the result against the community-standard KEGG library.
